title: Split Comma-Separated Tags and Count Frequency
description: Each product has a comma-separated `tags` column. **Split** the tags into individual rows and count how many products are associated with each tag. Show each tag and its product_count, ordered by frequency descending.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR(100), tags TEXT); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Laptop','electronics,computer,portable'),(2,'Phone','electronics,mobile,camera'),(3,'Tablet','electronics,portable,touchscreen'),(4,'Shirt','clothing,casual,cotton'),(5,'Shoes','clothing,footwear,sports');
solution_sql: SELECT TRIM(tag) AS tag, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products, LATERAL UNNEST(STRING_TO_ARRAY(tags, ',')) AS tag GROUP BY TRIM(tag) ORDER BY product_count DESC, tag

test_cases.description: 11 distinct tags. electronics=3, portable=2, clothing=2. All others appear once. Total 11 rows.

hints: Use STRING_TO_ARRAY(tags, ',') to convert the comma-separated string into a PostgreSQL array, then UNNEST to expand each array element into its own row.
Wrap tag in TRIM() to remove any leading/trailing whitespace before grouping.
explanation: STRING_TO_ARRAY splits the tags string on commas into an array (e.g., '{electronics,computer,portable}'). UNNEST expands this array into individual rows — one row per tag per product. After unnesting, all 5 products contribute 15 total tag rows. Grouping by trimmed tag and counting gives: electronics=3 (products 1,2,3), portable=2 (1,3), clothing=2 (4,5), and 8 other tags each appearing once — 11 distinct tags total.
